UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Make HWP limits compatible with legacy To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit a98b10da5fc5 ("Revert "UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Make HWP limits compatible with legacy"") due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' Under HWP the performance limits are calculated using max_perf_pct and min_perf_pct using possible performance, not available performance. The available performance can be reduced by no_turbo setting. To make compatible with legacy mode, use max/min performance percentage with respect to available performance. UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Calculate guaranteed performance for HWP To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit a2f7ced835c5 ("Revert "UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Calculate guaranteed performance for HWP"")' due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' When HWP is active, turbo activation ratio is not used to calculate max non turbo ratio. But on these systems the max non turbo ratio is decided by config TDP settings. This change removes usage of MSR_TURBO_ACTIVATION_RATIO for HWP systems, instead directly use TDP ratios, when more than one TDPs are available. BACKPORT: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Correct frequency setting in the HWP mode To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit b30f61089eaf ("Revert "BACKPORT: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Correct frequency setting in the HWP mode"")' due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' In the functions intel_pstate_hwp_set(), min/max range from HWP capability MSR along with max_perf_pct and min_perf_pct, is used to set the HWP request MSR. In some cases this doesn't result in the correct HWP max/min in HWP request. For example: In the following case: HWP capabilities from MSR 0x771 0x70a1220 Here cpufreq min/max frequencies from above MSR dump are 700MHz and 3.2GHz respectively. This will result in hwp_min = 0x07 hwp_max = 0x20 To limit max frequency to 2GHz: perf_limits->max_perf_pct = 63 (2GHz as a percent of 3.2GHz rounded up) With the current calculation: adj_range = max_perf_pct * range / 100; adj_range = 63 * (32 - 7) / 100 adj_range = 15 max = hw_min + adj_range; max = 7 + 15 = 22 This will result in HWP request of 0x160f, which will result in a frequency cap of 2.2GHz not 2GHz. The problem with the above calculation is that hwp_min of 7 is treated as 0% in the range. But max_perf_pct is calculated with respect to minimum as 0 and max as 3.2GHz or hwp_max, so adding hwp_min to it will result in more than the desired. Since the min_perf_pct and max_perf_pct is already a percent of max frequency or hwp_max, this min/max HWP request value can be calculated directly applying these percentage to hwp_max. Signed-off-by: Srinivas Pandruvada <srinivas.pandruvada@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 3f8ed54aee491bbb83656592c2d0ad7b78d045ca) Signed-off-by: Aditya Swarup <aditya.swarup@intel.com> Conflicts: drivers/cpufreq/intel_pstate.c Remove unused variables To avoid conflict in intel_pstate_hwp_set due to upstream linux 'commit eae48f046ffa ("cpufreq: intel_pstate: Per CPU P-State limits")' assign global perf limits variable to perf_limits Set min and max perf limit for hwp using perf_limits BUG=chrome-os-partner:61059 TEST=cd /sys/devices/system/cpu -> sysfs entry for intel_pstate/ iotools rdmsr 0(cpu no) 0x770 -> 1 (Intel HWP enabled) Run graphics_SanAngeles, performance doesn't regress by 20% Change-Id: I3e002e4d050de8c2902e2e5f7d08203e7b9ffadd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/487009 Commit-Ready: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Tested-by: Michael Cheng <michael.cheng@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Chintan M Patel <chintan.m.patel@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Puthikorn Voravootivat <puthik@chromium.org>

packager: Compare checksum before skipping tar in upload Earlier, we solely checked if a tarball was present before skipping the tarring of the autotest tarball. But this tarball might be stale. So, we additionally compare the checksum of the tarball against what checksum the pacakger dictionary has. If there is a mismatch, then we perform the tar again, and upload the new tarball (and update the corresponding checksum). This is a speculative patch. There doesn't seem to be a way to reproduce the Bug in question locally, and so this CL is being pushed. At the very least it should not lead to any further degradation in performance or functionality. Dump JMI not-aggregated dataset in a json file. While we can use aggregated files to determine performance regressions, we want to plot and analyse the collected JMI data in dedicated Google dashboards. This way, we can collect more signals about performance regressions. The CL adds a method that collects interesting metrics and dumps them in a raw format into a JSON file. This data can later be uploaded to CNS and be moved to CNS and fed into Google Dashboards. How to format the file to be digestible by the dashboards will be addressed separately.
